title: Attribute every workflow session’s published changes

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-418#attribute-every-workflow-session-record

**Verdict: Caught** (on the observed path: a closure whose completion receipt stops retirement).

**Next proof action:** none needed for this fault. Optionally, add a remote-tip assertion (`lsRemoteSha(fixture.origin, main) === final`, or "no session record commit on origin") to the two looped completion-gate cases. Right now they catch the fault only because the record commit also moves the local branch.

## What was checked
- **Story and revision:** `.planning/seeds/SEED-418-review-published-session-changes.md#attribute-every-workflow-session-record`, plan `747-attribute-every-workflow-session-record`, revision `edd885dabbe96fa3482d86cf9d8e8e19f54d6449`, branch `claude/attribute-every-workflow-session-s-published-cha-2`.
- **Promise:** publish one record for the session's accepted work at Story Wrap-up. Trunk Mode `finish` publishes it only after the accepted final closure's completion receipt permits retirement. No record is published when completion stops the close.
- **Why this fault:** this is the caller's "record pushed when the closure was not accepted" candidate. The execution swapped exact trunk-tip checks for `targetHolds` (ancestry) checks, and push counts now ignore record commits (`countClosurePushes`). Those changes could hide an extra record commit on the target, and the completion stop is where such a commit would be wrong.
- **Fault:** in `Distribution/src/skills/dough-story-wrap-up/scripts/trunk-closure.mjs`, the `!receiptPermitsRetirement(completion)` branch was changed to `await publishClosureRecord(closure, { observation, completion })` before it returns `{ stopped: "completion", ... }`. The record is sealed and published even though completion stopped. Fixtures and assertions were left unchanged.
- **Maintained checks examined:**
  - `Distribution/tests/skills/dough-story-wrap-up/trunk-closure-completion-gate.test.mjs`: 3 cases (failed CI receipt, success with retained shutdown, no CI verdict).
  - `Distribution/tests/skills/dough-story-wrap-up/trunk-closure-session-record.test.mjs`: 2 cases (refused record push, failing record commit, each with a rerun).

## Runs
- **Setup:** a scratch detached worktree of the revision under `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/e3e1db8d/tmp/ic-scratch`, with `node_modules` symlinked from the execution checkout. Before the probe it was clean apart from that symlink. The execution checkout was not modified.
- **Command:** `env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_CASE_OUTCOMES=... npm test -- <the two files>`.
- **Baseline:** exit 0. The case-outcomes file showed 5/5 passed (3 completion-gate, 2 session-record), so the checks really ran.
- **Independent witness (scratch test, deleted afterwards):** the failed-CI scenario under the fault returned `code 1, step "completion"`. The origin `main` tip was `60e2d3e…`, not the final closure `fddbd0a…`, and `sessionRecordCommits(origin)` held exactly that tip. So a session record was published on trunk while the closure's completion stopped the close. That is the wrong behavior on the intended path.
- **Faulted run:** exit 1. All 3 completion-gate cases failed and both session-record cases still passed (they do not exercise this path).
  - The catching assertion was `assert.equal(await branchSha(fixture), final)`: line 49 in the looped failed-CI and retained-shutdown cases, line 83 in the no-verdict case. The actual value was the record commit's SHA.
  - The no-verdict case's remote check, `assert.equal(await lsRemoteSha(fixture.origin, main), final)` at line 84, would also catch it, but the run stopped at line 83 first.
  - The catch works because the record commit moves the local execution branch before it is pushed. The two looped cases have no remote-tip assertion.
- **Restoration:** `git checkout` of the faulted file and deletion of the witness file. `git status --porcelain` showed only the `node_modules` symlink, the same as before the probe, and `git diff` was empty. The rerun of the same command exited 0 with 5/5 passed. The scratch worktree was then removed and pruned. `git worktree list` no longer lists it, and the execution checkout status is clean.

## Gaps and notes (not verdicts)
- Only one fault was applied. The other caller candidates were not probed:
  - a second record commit, or a second closure push, on rerun;
  - the record commit inside its own ranges;
  - a refused candidate or another writer's commit entering a range;
  - no record at all on a normal finish.
- Inspection only, not a faulted observation: no Trunk Mode test that checks record ranges has another writer advance trunk just before the final closure. `trunk-closure.test.mjs` and `trunk-closure-rebased-rerun.test.mjs` have such writers but use `targetHolds` and do not read the record. A fault in the closure pair's base for that case is therefore not known to be covered. This is insufficient evidence, not a confirmed missing path.
- `countClosurePushes` ignores record commits on origin, so an extra record push in the closure tests would rest on the record-specific tests. This was not probed.

## Cost
- **Test runtime (measured, wall seconds from the run helper):** baseline 36 s, faulted 36 s, restored 36 s. Per-file runner times: completion-gate 35.8 s / 36.7 s, session-record 6.9 s / 6.5 s. Witness `node --test` run: about 20–30 s (estimated; not timed separately).
- **Human effort:** unavailable. No human took part in this worker run.
- **Agent effort:** unavailable. No token or turn meter is exposed to this worker. About 25 tool calls (counted from this session; agent-reported).


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 309369 ms (measured), from 1795311949813 to 1795312259182 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision edd885dabbe96fa3482d86cf9d8e8e19f54d6449: verdict Caught; no follow-up.
